policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: euthys/eutheos are orthographic variants of the same adverb; ASV 'straightway' renders either.
ASV 'whereon no man ever yet sat' renders oupo with 'yet'; the omitting reading leaves nothing for it.
ASV 'sat' is a plain past that renders the aorist ekathisen and the perfect kekathiken alike, especially after 'never yet'.
ASV 'loose him, and bring him' is two coordinate imperatives joined by 'and'; the alternative has a participle 'having loosed him' plus one imperative.
Recitative hoti before direct speech is untranslated in ASV; its presence or absence leaves no English trace.
euthys/eutheos are orthographic variants of the same adverb; ASV 'straightway' renders either.
ASV 'will send him back hither' renders palin with 'back', and the margin 'Or, again' offers the other rendering of that same word; the omitting reading gives it nothing to render.
ASV opens 'And they went away' with kai, not the postpositive de of the alternative.
The variant is the article with thyran; ASV 'at the door' supplies the English article either way.
ASV 'even as Jesus had said' renders eipen; eneteilato would be 'commanded'.
ASV 'they bring the colt' is the historic present pherousin; egagon would be 'they brought'.
English 'cast' is identical in present and past, so ASV 'and cast on him their garments' does not separate epiballousin from epebalon.
The variant is the case of the pronoun after epiball-; ASV 'cast on him' renders accusative and dative alike.
ASV 'And many spread' begins with kai; the alternative has 'Many' with postpositive de.
ASV 'branches, which they had cut from the fields' renders kopsantes ek ton agron; the alternative reads 'from the trees' and adds 'and spread them in the way', neither of which the ASV has.
ASV 'cried, Hosanna' has no 'saying' answering the added legontes.
ASV 'Blessed is the kingdom that cometh, the kingdom of our father David' lacks the added 'in the name of the Lord' after 'kingdom'.
ASV 'And he entered into Jerusalem, into the temple' names no subject and does not coordinate the two places; the alternative adds 'Jesus, and'.
opse and opsias both give the time phrase ASV renders 'it being now eventide'.
apo makrothen and bare makrothen are both 'afar off' in ASV.
The variant is only the order of ti and heuresei; ASV 'he might find anything thereon' follows English order regardless.
Both readings say the season was not; ASV 'for it was not the season of figs' does not show the article or the placement of the negative.
ASV 'And he answered and said unto it' has the pronoun, not the added subject 'Jesus'.
The variant is only the order of 'for ever' and 'from thee'; ASV 'fruit from thee henceforward for ever' arranges the phrases by English idiom.
ASV 'and he entered into the temple' uses a pronoun where the alternative adds the subject 'Jesus'.
The variant is the article before the second participle; ASV 'them that sold and them that bought' supplies the English pronoun either way.
ASV 'And he taught, and said unto them' is a second finite verb joined by 'and'; the alternative has the participle 'saying'.
ASV 'said unto them' renders autois, which the omitting reading lacks.
ASV 'ye have made it a den of robbers' is a perfect answering pepoiekate, not the aorist epoiesate.
ASV 'the chief priests and the scribes' keeps the base order of the two nouns; the alternative reverses them.
gar and hoti are both rendered 'for' in ASV 'for all the multitude was astonished'.
The ASV note 'Greek whenever evening came' renders the indefinite hotan; hote would be 'when'.
ASV text reads 'he went forth out of the city', the singular exeporeueto, and its note 'Some ancient authorities read they' assigns the plural to the margin.
The variant is only the order of proi and the participle; ASV 'as they passed by in the morning' follows English order.
ASV 'Verily I say unto you' has no 'for' answering the added gar.
ASV 'but shall believe' renders present and aorist subjunctive alike.
ASV 'believe that what he saith cometh to pass; he shall have it' ends there, without the alternative's added 'whatsoever he saith'; the remaining two readings differ only in punctuation spacing.
ASV 'whatsoever ye pray and ask for' is two coordinate verbs; the alternative has 'praying' as a participle subordinate to 'ye ask'.
The ASV note 'Greek received' gives the aorist elabete; lambanete would be 'receive'.
ASV 'whensoever ye stand praying' renders either form of the verb after hotan.
ASV ends the verse at 'your trespasses' and its note says 'Many ancient authorities add verse 26', putting the added sentence in the margin, not the text.
ASV 'and they said unto him' is past, answering the imperfect elegon; legousin would be the historic present 'they say', as ASV renders it in verse 33.
ASV 'or who gave thee this authority' renders the disjunctive e, not kai.
The variant is only the placement of edoken; ASV 'who gave thee this authority' must put verb before object in English.
ASV 'And Jesus said unto them' has no 'answered' for the added apokritheis.
ASV 'I will ask of you one question' lacks the 'I also' of the added kai ego.
The variant is the article with the baptism of John; ASV 'The baptism of John' supplies the English article either way.
ASV 'they reasoned with themselves' renders the simple and compound verb alike.
ASV goes straight from 'saying' to 'If we shall say, From heaven', with no 'What shall we say?' — the omitting reading.
ASV 'Why then did ye not believe him?' renders oun with 'then'; the omitting reading leaves it unaccounted for.
ASV 'they feared the people' uses 'people', its rendering of laos; ochlos it renders 'multitude'.
The variant is only the order of ontos and hoti; ASV 'for all verily held John to be a prophet' shows no order.
The variant is only the placement of 'to Jesus'; ASV 'And they answered Jesus and say' arranges it by English idiom.
ASV 'And Jesus saith unto them' has no 'answering' for the added apokritheis.
